title: C5 admission and dense-rank scaling audit
question: Does dense-CDL rank continue toward linear growth at M=2048,4096,8192, and can explicit OR-LSH table-count scaling recover the valid candidates admitted by the calibrated dense K90 shortlist at M=1024?
hypothesis: The dense rank curve will show increasing local P90 exponents at higher M, while explicit LSH table scaling will expose a recall/compute frontier that is hidden by the current m^rho table rule.

arms.name: dense_scaling
arms.intervention: extend the same leakage-corrected noisy CDL router to M=2048,4096,8192 without changing training

arms.name: lsh_table_sweep
arms.intervention: fixed noisy CDL representation with OR-LSH tables swept over 1,2,4,8,10,12,16,24,32,48,64 at M=1024

held_constant: same CDL learner, latent dimension, learning rate, training steps, and train M distribution
same candidate duplication factor per class
same OR-LSH random-hyperplane family within a sweep
same held-out trial stream per seed
no persistent state input to the main arm
no hidden-target input to the router

decision_rule.condition: Report local P90 rank exponents for every consecutive M doubling and fit the full-range exponent.
decision_rule.licenses: descriptive dense-CDL scaling behavior on the registered synthetic workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: a sublinear claim when the local exponent trends toward 1, or any theorem.

decision_rule.condition: Report every registered LSH table count, including the calibration-derived iid L90 diagnostic, without selecting an operating point from held-out outcomes.
decision_rule.licenses: an admission recall versus reranking-work curve for the fixed representation.
decision_rule.does_not_license: claim that a specific L is optimal without a separately registered operating-point rule.

scientific_gates: The Hamming reference is treated as a routing solvability reference, not as evidence of learned semantic retrieval.
The main arm has no persistent state input; persistence remains untested by this audit.
The sweep cap is 128 and the maximum requested table count is 64, so the intervention is unbound by the cap.
